units.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人。
units.en: Ding Hui, whose style name was Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.
units.literal: Ding Hui, style name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shou Prefecture.

units.zh: 父季。
units.en: His father was named Ji.
units.literal: His father was Ji.

units.zh: 會幼放蕩縱橫，不治農產，恒隨哀挽者學紼謳，尤嗜其聲。
units.en: In youth Ding Hui was unruly and idle, neglected the family fields, and constantly trailed funeral parties to learn mourning dirges for the pall ropes; he loved their cadence above all else.
units.literal: As a youth Hui was wild and unrestrained, did not tend the family farms, always followed funeral mourners to learn pall-rope dirges, and was especially fond of their sound.

units.zh: 既長，遇亂，合雄兒為盜，有誌功名。
units.en: When he came of age amid the chaos, he gathered bold companions and turned bandit, yet he burned to win a name in arms.
units.literal: When grown he met turmoil, gathered bold fellows and became a bandit, and harbored ambition for meritorious achievement.

units.zh: 黃巢渡淮，會從梁祖為部曲，梁祖鎮門，會曆都押衙。
units.en: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, Ding Hui entered the Liang Founder's personal command. After the Founder secured the capital, Hui rose to chief of the capital guard office.
units.literal: When Huang Chao crossed the Huai, Hui followed the Liang Founder as a soldier in his personal command; when the Founder held the capital gate, Hui rose through the post of chief capital guard officer.

units.zh: 自梁祖誅宗權，並時溥，屠朱瑄，走朱瑾，會恒以兵從，多立奇功。
units.en: From the Founder's execution of Qin Zongquan through his absorption of Shi Pu, the slaughter of Zhu Xuan, and the rout of Zhu Jin, Ding Hui marched at his side and won repeated striking victories.
units.literal: From when the Founder executed Zongquan, annexed Shi Pu, slaughtered Zhu Xuan, and drove off Zhu Jin, Hui constantly followed with troops and established many brilliant achievements.

units.zh: 文德中，表授懷州刺史，曆滑州留後、河陽節度使、檢校司徒。
units.en: During the Wende reign he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai, then served as acting governor of Hua, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting Minister of the Masses.
units.literal: In the Wende era he was appointed by memorial as prefect of Huai Prefecture, then served as acting governor of Hua Prefecture, military commissioner of Heyang, and acting minister of the masses.

units.zh: 自河陽以疾致政於洛陽。
units.en: He left Heyang on grounds of illness and retired to Luoyang.
units.literal: From Heyang he retired because of illness and settled in Luoyang.

units.zh: 梁祖季年猜忌，故將功大者多遭族滅，會陰有避禍之志，稱疾者累年。
units.en: In his last years the Liang Founder grew suspicious, and veteran commanders of great merit were often wiped out to the last kinsman. Ding Hui quietly resolved to escape that fate and pleaded illness year after year.
units.literal: In the Founder's declining years he grew suspicious; therefore old commanders of great merit were mostly exterminated by clan purge. Hui secretly harbored the wish to escape calamity and claimed illness for many years.

units.zh: 天復元年，梁祖奄有河中、晉、絳，乃起會為昭義節度使。
units.en: In the first year of Tianfu, after the Founder seized Hedong, Jin, and Jiang, he recalled Ding Hui and made him military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianfu the Founder suddenly held Hedong, Jin, and Jiang, then summoned Hui back as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 昭宗幸洛陽，加同平章事。
units.en: When Emperor Zhaozong came to Luoyang, Ding Hui was made a joint manager of government affairs.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong visited Luoyang, Hui was made Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court.

units.zh: 其年，昭宗遇弑，哀問至，會三軍縞素，流涕久之。
units.en: That same year, when word came that Zhaozong had been murdered, Ding Hui's whole army put on white mourning and wept for a long while.
units.literal: That year, when Zhaozong was assassinated, the tidings of mourning arrived; Hui's entire army donned white mourning and wept for a long time.

units.zh: 時梁祖親討劉守文於滄州，駐軍於長蘆。
units.en: The Liang Founder was then campaigning in person against Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and had encamped at Changlu.
units.literal: At the time the Founder was personally campaigning against Liu Shouwen at Cang Prefecture and camped his army at Changlu.

units.zh: 三年十二月，王師攻會，居旬日，會以潞州歸於武皇。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army besieged him; within ten days Ding Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year the imperial army attacked Hui; within ten days Hui surrendered Luzhou to the Martial Sovereign.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：梁祖雄猜，疑忌功臣，忽謂敬翔曰：「吾夢丁會在前祗候，吾將乘馬欲出，圉人以馬就台，忽為丁會跨之以出，時夢中怒，叱喝數聲，因驚覺，甚惡之。」
units.en: (According to the 《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》: The Liang Founder was fierce, suspicious, and wary of his great commanders. One day he suddenly told Jing Xiang, "I dreamed that Ding Hui was waiting before me as I prepared to mount and ride out. The groom led the horse to the terrace, and in the dream Ding Hui vaulted onto it and rode out with me. I shouted at him in anger several times, then woke—and the omen filled me with loathing.")
units.literal: (《Miscellaneous Sayings of the Northern Dreams》 states: The Founder was fierce and suspicious and wary of meritorious commanders. Suddenly he said to Jing Xiang: "I dreamed Ding Hui was attending in front of me. I was about to mount my horse to go out when the groom brought the horse to the terrace. Suddenly Ding Hui straddled it and rode out with me. In the dream I grew angry and shouted several times, then awoke, and greatly detested it."

units.zh: 是月，丁會舉潞州軍民歸河東矣。）〉
units.en: That very month Ding Hui brought the army and people of Luzhou over to Hedong.)〉
units.literal: That month Ding Hui led the Luzhou army and people over to Hedong.)〉

units.zh: 引見，會泣曰：「臣非不能守潞，但以汴王篡弱唐祚，猜嫌舊將，臣雖蒙保薦之恩，而不忍相從，今所謂吐盜父之食以見王也。」
units.en: When he was received in audience Ding Hui wept and said, "It is not that I could not hold Luzhou. The Prince of Bian has usurped and enfeebled the Tang house and now suspects every old commander. Though I owed him the grace of preservation, I could not bear to follow him further. What I do now is what they call vomiting out a robber father's food to show oneself before the true king."
units.literal: When presented in audience Hui wept and said: "Your subject is not incapable of holding Luzhou, but because the Prince of Bian usurped and weakened the Tang succession and is suspicious of old commanders, though I received the grace of preservation I could not bear to follow him—what is now called vomiting what one's robber father fed one to show the king."

units.zh: 武皇納之，賜甲第於太原，位在諸將上。
units.en: The Martial Sovereign welcomed him, granted him a great mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.
units.literal: The Martial Sovereign accepted him, granted him a mansion in Taiyuan, and ranked him above the other generals.

units.zh: 五年，汴將李思安圍潞州，以會為都招討使、檢校太尉。
units.en: In the fifth year the Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou, and Ding Hui was made chief campaign commander with the acting rank of Grand Commandant.
units.literal: In the fifth year Bian general Li Si'an besieged Luzhou; Hui was made chief campaign commander and acting grand commandant.

units.zh: 莊宗嗣王位，與會決謀，破汴軍於夾城。
units.en: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the kingship he took counsel with Ding Hui and shattered the Bian army at Jiacheng.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded to the kingship he joined with Hui in council and shattered the Bian army at Jiacheng.

units.zh: 七年十一月，卒於大原。
units.en: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he died at Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year he died at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 莊宗即位，追贈太師。
units.en: After Zhuangzong took the throne, Ding Hui was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 有子七人，知沆為梁祖所誅，餘皆曆內職。
units.en: He had seven sons. Zhihang was executed by the Liang Founder; the rest all rose through inner court offices.
units.literal: He had seven sons; Zhihang was executed by the Liang Founder, the rest all held inner court posts.

units.zh: 閻寶，字瓊美，鄆州人。
units.en: Yan Bao, whose style name was Qiongmei, came from Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: Yan Bao, style name Qiongmei, was a native of Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 父佐，海州刺史。
units.en: His father Zuo had served as prefect of Hai Prefecture.
units.literal: His father Zuo was prefect of Hai Prefecture.

units.zh: 寶少事朱瑾為牙將，瑾之失守於兗也，寶與瑾將胡規、康懷英歸汴梁，皆擢任之。
units.en: In youth Yan Bao served Zhu Jin as a guard officer. When Jin lost Yanzhou, Bao went with Jin's officers Hu Gui and Kang Huaiying to Bianliang, and the Liang court promoted them all.
units.literal: In youth Bao served Zhu Jin as a guard officer; when Jin lost Yan Prefecture, Bao with Jin's generals Hu Gui and Kang Huaiying returned to Bianliang, and all were promoted and employed.

units.zh: 自梁祖陳師河朔，爭霸關西，寶與葛從周、丁會、賀德倫、李思安各為大將，統兵四出，所至立功，曆洺、隨、宿、鄭四州刺史。
units.en: From the Founder's campaigns in the Hebei north through his struggle for the northwest, Yan Bao stood with Ge Congzhou, Ding Hui, He Delun, and Li Si'an among the great commanders. They led armies on every front, won merit wherever they marched, and Yan Bao in turn held the prefectures of Ming, Sui, Su, and Zheng.
units.literal: From when the Founder arrayed troops in the Hebei region and contended for supremacy in the Guanxi region, Bao with Ge Congzhou, Ding Hui, He Delun, and Li Si'an each served as great generals, commanded armies in four directions, won merit wherever they went, and served as prefect of Ming, Sui, Su, and Zheng prefectures.

units.zh: 天祐六年，梁祖以寶為邢洺節度使、檢校太傅。
units.en: In the sixth year of Tianyou the Liang Founder made Yan Bao military commissioner of Xing and Ming with the acting rank of Grand Mentor.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Tianyou the Founder made Bao military commissioner of Xing and Ming and acting grand mentor.

units.zh: 莊宗定魏博，十三年，攻相、衛、洺、磁，下之，寶獨保邢州，城孤援絕。
units.en: After Zhuangzong secured Weibo, in the thirteenth year he took Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Ci. Yan Bao alone still held Xingzhou, his city isolated and his relief cut off.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Weibo, in the thirteenth year he attacked Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Ci and took them; Bao alone held Xing Prefecture, the city isolated and reinforcements cut off.

units.zh: 八月，寶以邢州降，莊宗嘉之，進位檢校太尉、同平章事，遙領天平軍節度使、東南面招討等使，待以賓禮，位在諸將上，每有謀畫，與之參決。
units.en: In the eighth month Yan Bao surrendered Xingzhou. Zhuangzong praised him, raised him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, and gave him titular command of Tianping and the southeastern campaign, treating him as an honored guest and ranking him above the other generals. On every major plan Zhuangzong consulted him and followed his counsel.
units.literal: In the eighth month Bao surrendered Xing Prefecture; Zhuangzong praised him, advanced him to acting Grand Commandant and Grand Councilor, made him titular military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner, treated him with guest ceremony, ranked him above the other generals, and whenever there was planning consulted and decided with him.

units.zh: 契丹之寇幽州也，周德威危急，寶與李存審從明宗擊契丹於幽州西北，解圍而還。
units.en: When the Khitan besieged Youzhou and Zhou Dewei was hard pressed, Yan Bao and Li Cunshen followed Mingzong to strike the Khitan northwest of the city, broke the siege, and returned.
units.literal: When the Khitan raided You Prefecture and Zhou Dewei was in peril, Bao with Li Cunshen followed Mingzong to strike the Khitan northwest of You Prefecture, lifted the siege, and returned.

units.zh: 胡柳之役，諸軍逗撓，汴軍登無石山，其勢甚盛。
units.en: At the battle of Huliu the allied armies hung back while the Bian forces took Wushi Mountain and gathered overwhelming strength.
units.literal: At the battle of Huliu the armies hesitated and hung back; the Bian army climbed Wushi Mountain and their momentum was very strong.

units.zh: 莊宗望之，畏其不敵，且欲保營。
units.en: Zhuangzong looked on them, feared he could not prevail, and thought only of holding his camp.
units.literal: Zhuangzong looked at them, feared he could not match them, and wished moreover to preserve the camp.

units.zh: 寶進曰：「王深入敵境，偏師不利，王彥章騎軍已入濮州，山下唯列步兵，向晚皆有歸誌。
units.en: Yan Bao stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty has marched deep into enemy country, and one wing has already faltered. Wang Yanzhang's cavalry has entered Puzhou; below the mountain they have posted only foot soldiers, and by evening every man will be thinking of home.
units.literal: Bao advanced and said: "Your Majesty has penetrated deep into enemy territory; a detached force has met misfortune. Wang Yanzhang's cavalry has already entered Pu Prefecture; below the mountain they have only arrayed foot soldiers, and toward evening all will have the will to return.

units.zh: 我盡銳擊之，敗走必矣。
units.en: If we throw our best troops against them, they are sure to break and run.
units.literal: If we strike them with all our elite troops, they will surely flee in defeat.

units.zh: 今若引退，必為所乘，我軍未集，更聞賊勝，即不戰而自潰也。
units.en: If we pull back now they will surely overtake us. Our forces are not yet fully assembled, and once the men hear the enemy has won they will scatter without a fight.
units.literal: If we now withdraw we will surely be overtaken by them; our army is not yet gathered, and if we further hear the enemy has won, we will collapse without fighting.

units.zh: 凡決勝料情，情勢已得，斷在不疑。
units.en: Victory always turns on reading the moment aright; once the odds are in hand, the decisive thing is not to hesitate.
units.literal: In all cases of deciding victory and gauging circumstances, once the situation and momentum are obtained, the decision lies in not hesitating.

units.zh: 今王之成敗，在此一戰，若不決勝，設使餘眾渡河，河朔非王有也，王其勉之！」
units.en: Your Majesty's fate now hangs on this single battle. If we fail to win it here, and the rest of their army crosses the river, the north will no longer be yours. Press the fight, sire!"
units.literal: Now Your Majesty's success or failure lies in this one battle; if we do not decide victory, suppose the remaining masses cross the river—the Hebei north will not be Your Majesty's; Your Majesty must exert yourself!"

units.zh: 莊宗聞之聳聽，曰：「微公幾失計。」
units.en: Zhuangzong listened with rising attention and said, "Without you I would nearly have thrown the campaign away."
units.literal: Zhuangzong heard and straightened to listen, saying: "Without you I would nearly have lost the plan."

units.zh: 即引騎大噪，奮槊登山，大敗汴人。
units.en: He at once led his cavalry forward with a great shout, drove his spears up the slope, and routed the Bian army.
units.literal: He immediately led cavalry in great clamor, brandished spears and climbed the mountain, and greatly defeated the Bian men.

units.zh: 十八年，張文禮殺王鎔叛，寶帥師進討。
units.en: In the eighteenth year Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong and rebelled; Yan Bao marched to suppress him.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year Zhang Wenli killed Wang Rong and rebelled; Bao led troops forward to attack.

units.zh: 八月，收趙州，進渡滹水，擒賊黨張友順以獻。
units.en: In the eighth month he recovered Zhao Prefecture, crossed the Hutuo, and captured the rebel partisan Zhang Youshun for presentation to the throne.
units.literal: In the eighth month he recovered Zhao Prefecture, advanced and crossed the Hutuo River, and captured the rebel partisan Zhang Youshun to present.

units.zh: 九月，進逼真定，結營西南隅。
units.en: In the ninth month he pressed Zhending and pitched camp at the city's southwest corner.
units.literal: In the ninth month he advanced pressing Zhending and encamped at the southwest corner.

units.zh: 掘塹柵以環之，決大悲寺漕渠以浸其郛。
units.en: He dug trenches and palisades to ring the city and breached the Dabei Temple canal to flood the outer walls.
units.literal: He dug moats and stockades to encircle it and breached the canal of Dabei Temple to flood the outer wall.

units.zh: 十九年正月，契丹三十萬來援鎮州，前鋒至新樂，眾心憂之。
units.en: In the first month of the nineteenth year three hundred thousand Khitan marched to relieve Zhenzhou; when their vanguard reached Xinle the army's spirits sank.
units.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year three hundred thousand Khitan came to aid Zhen Prefecture; the vanguard reached Xinle and the army's hearts were anxious.

units.zh: 寶見莊宗，指陳方略，軍情乃安。
units.en: Yan Bao laid out his plan before Zhuangzong, and the army's morale steadied.
units.literal: Bao saw Zhuangzong, pointed out and laid out strategy, and the army's mood then settled.

units.zh: 敵退，加檢校侍中。
units.en: After the enemy withdrew he was promoted to acting Palace Attendant.
units.literal: When the enemy withdrew he was advanced to acting palace attendant.

units.zh: 三月，城中饑，王處瑾之眾出城求食，寶縱其出，伏兵截擊之。
units.en: In the third month famine gripped the city. Wang Chujin's men came out to forage; Yan Bao let them leave the gates, then ambushed and cut them down.
units.literal: In the third month the city was starving; Wang Chujin's masses went out of the city to seek food; Bao let them out and ambush troops intercepted and struck them.

units.zh: 饑賊大至，諸軍未集，為賊年乘；
units.en: The starving rebels came in force before the allied armies had fully gathered, and Yan Bao's men were overrun;
units.literal: The starving enemy came in great numbers; the armies were not yet gathered and were overrun by the enemy;

units.zh: 寶乃收軍退保趙州，因慚憤成疾，疽發背而卒，時年六十。
units.en: Yan Bao drew his troops back to Zhao Prefecture. Shame and anger brought on illness; a carbuncle broke out between his shoulders and he died at the age of sixty.
units.literal: Bao then gathered the army, withdrew to hold Zhao Prefecture, and because of shame and anger fell ill; a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died, aged sixty.

units.zh: 同光初，追贈太師；
units.en: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was posthumously granted the honor of Grand Preceptor;

units.zh: 晉天福中，追封太原郡王。
units.en: and under Jin in the Tianfu era he was posthumously created Prince of Taiyuan.
units.literal: in the Tianfu era of Jin he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Taiyuan Commandery.

units.zh: 有子八人，宏倫、宏儒皆位至郡守。
units.en: He had eight sons; Honglun and Hongru both rose to commandery prefect.
units.literal: He had eight sons; Honglun and Hongru both reached posts as commandery prefects.

units.zh: 符習，趙州昭慶縣人。
units.en: Fu Xi came from Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.
units.literal: Fu Xi, a native of Zhaoqing County in Zhao Prefecture.

units.zh: 少從軍，事節度使王鎔，積功至列校。
units.en: He entered the army young, served the Zhao military commissioner Wang Rong, and by steady merit rose to regimental commander.
units.literal: In youth he entered the army, served Military Commissioner Wang Rong, and through accumulated merit rose to regimental commander.

units.zh: 自莊宗經略河朔，與鎔連衡，常令習率師從莊宗征討。
units.en: Once Zhuangzong began his campaigns in the Hebei north and allied with Wang Rong, he regularly ordered Fu Xi to lead Zhao troops on Zhuangzong's campaigns.
units.literal: From when Zhuangzong planned the Hebei north and allied with Rong, he constantly ordered Xi to lead troops following Zhuangzong in campaigns.

units.zh: 鎔為張文禮所害，時習在德勝寨，文禮上書請習等歸鎮。
units.en: When Wang Rong was murdered by Zhang Wenli, Fu Xi was at Desheng Stockade. Wenli wrote asking Xi and his officers to return to Zhao.
units.literal: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli, at the time Xi was at Desheng Stockade; Wenli sent a letter requesting Xi and others return to the commandery.

units.zh: 習雨泣訴於莊宗曰：「臣本趙人，家世事王氏，故使嘗授臣一劍，俾臣平蕩凶寇。
units.en: Fu Xi wept bitterly before Zhuangzong and said, "I am a man of Zhao. For generations my house served the Wang family. The late lord once gave me a sword and charged me to crush the murderers.
units.literal: Xi wept in the rain and appealed to Zhuangzong, saying: "Your subject is originally a man of Zhao; for generations my family served the Wang house. The late lord once bestowed on your subject one sword, ordering your subject to pacify and sweep away the fierce bandits.

units.zh: 自聞變故，徒懷冤憤，欲以自剄，無益於營魂。
units.en: Since I heard what befell him I have lived only with outrage. I might cut my own throat, but that would do my dead lord's spirit no good.
units.literal: Since hearing of the calamity I have only harbored grievance and rage, wishing to cut my own throat, which would be of no benefit to the late lord's spirit.

units.zh: 且張文禮乃幽、滄叛將，趙王知人不盡，過意任使，致被反噬。
units.en: Zhang Wenli was a turncoat from You and Cang. The Prince of Zhao misjudged him, trusted him too far, and was destroyed for it.
units.literal: Moreover Zhang Wenli is a rebel general of You and Cang; the Prince of Zhao did not fully know men, excessively trusted and employed him, and thus was bitten in return.

units.zh: 臣雖不武，願在霸府血戰而死，不能委身於凶首。」
units.en: I am no great warrior, but I would rather die fighting in your service than submit to that murderer."
units.literal: Though your subject is not martial, I wish to die fighting bloodily in the hegemon's court and cannot entrust my person to the murderous chief."

units.zh: 莊宗曰：「爾既懷舊君之愛，可復仇乎？
units.en: Zhuangzong said, "If you still love your old master, will you take revenge?
units.literal: Zhuangzong said: "Since you cherish love for your old lord, can you take revenge?

units.zh: 吾當助爾。」
units.en: I will help you do it."
units.literal: I shall assist you."

units.zh: 習等舉身投地，號慟感激，謝曰：「王必以故使輔翼之勞，雪其冤恥，臣不敢期師旅為助，但悉本軍可以誅其逆豎。」
units.en: Fu Xi and his officers prostrated themselves, wept in gratitude, and said, "If Your Majesty will honor our late lord's service and avenge his death, I do not ask for a great host—only let my own Zhao troops strike down the traitor."
units.literal: Xi and the others threw their bodies to the ground, wailed in grief with gratitude, and thanked him, saying: "Your Majesty will surely, because of the late lord's labor in assisting, wipe away his grievance and shame; your subject does not dare expect army support, only that the entire native army can execute the rebellious villain."

units.zh: 莊宗即令閻寶、史建瑭助習討文禮，乃以習為成德軍兵馬留後。
units.en: Zhuangzong at once ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to aid Fu Xi against Wenli and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.
units.literal: Zhuangzong immediately ordered Yan Bao and Shi Jiantang to assist Xi in attacking Wenli, and made Xi acting military governor of the Chengde army.

units.zh: 及文禮誅，將正授節鉞，習不敢當其任，辭曰：「臣緣故使未葬，又無嗣息，臣合服斬縗，候臣禮制畢聽命。」
units.en: After Wenli was killed, Zhuangzong was ready to grant Fu Xi the full commission, but Xi declined. "My late lord is still unburied and left no heir," he said. "I ought to wear the deepest mourning. When those rites are finished I will await your command."
units.literal: When Wenli was executed and Xi was about to receive the formal commission of command, Xi did not dare undertake the post and declined, saying: "Because the late lord is not yet buried and there is no heir, your subject ought to wear the hemp of deepest mourning; when your subject's ritual obligations are finished I shall await orders."

units.zh: 及莊宗兼領鎮州，乃割相、衛二州置義寧軍，以習為節度使。
units.en: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhenzhou, he carved out Xiang and Wei to form the Yining command and made Fu Xi its military commissioner.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong also took charge of Zhen Prefecture, he carved out Xiang and Wei prefectures to establish the Yining army and made Xi its military commissioner.

units.zh: 習奏曰：「 魏博六州，見係霸府，不宜遽有割隸。
units.en: Fu Xi memorialized, "The six prefectures of Weibo already belong to your hegemony and ought not be carved away so soon.
units.literal: Xi memorialized, saying: "The six prefectures of Weibo are now tied to the hegemon's court and ought not suddenly to have territory carved away.

units.zh: 但授臣河南一鎮，臣自攻取。」
units.en: Grant me only one command south of the Yellow River, and I will take it myself."
units.literal: Only grant your subject one commandery south of the river and your subject will seize it himself."

units.zh: 乃授天平軍節度、東南面招討使。
units.en: He was then made military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner.
units.literal: He was then granted military commissioner of Tianping and southeastern campaign commissioner.

units.zh: 習有器度，性忠壯，自莊宗十年沿河戰守，習常以本軍從，心無顧望，諸將服其為人。
units.en: Fu Xi was broad-minded and steadfast. For ten years along the Yellow River he marched with Zhuangzong at the head of his Zhao troops, never wavering, and the other commanders respected him for it.
units.literal: Xi had capacity and breadth, his nature loyal and stalwart; from Zhuangzong's tenth year along the river in battle and defense Xi constantly led the native army in attendance, his heart without looking back, and the generals admired his character.

units.zh: 同光初，以習為邢州節度。
units.en: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was made military commissioner of Xingzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang Xi was made military commissioner of Xing Prefecture.

units.zh: 明年，移鎮青州。
units.en: The following year he was transferred to Qingzhou.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred to garrison Qing Prefecture.

units.zh: 四年二月，趙在禮盜據魏州，習受詔以淄、青之師進討；
units.en: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili seized Weizhou by force. Fu Xi was ordered to march from Zi and Qing to suppress him;
units.literal: In the second month of the fourth year Zhao Zaili seized We Prefecture by theft; Xi received the edict to advance with the Zi and Qing armies to attack;

units.zh: 至則會軍亂，習乃退軍渡河。
units.en: but when he arrived the allied camp was already in revolt, and he drew his army back across the river.
units.literal: when he arrived the assembled armies were in turmoil, and Xi then withdrew the army and crossed the river.

units.zh: 明宗自鄴赴洛，遣使召之，習不時而至。
units.en: Mingzong marched from Ye to Luoyang and sent for him, but Fu Xi did not come at once.
units.literal: Mingzong went from Ye to Luoyang and sent envoys to summon him; Xi did not arrive in timely fashion.

units.zh: 既至，謁明宗於胙縣。
units.en: When he did arrive he presented himself to Mingzong at Zuo County.
units.literal: When he arrived he paid respects to Mingzong at Zuo County.

units.zh: 霍彥威謂習曰：「主上所知者十人，公在其四，何猶豫乎！」
units.en: Huo Yanwei told him, "Of the ten men our lord knows, you are the fourth—why still hesitate?"
units.literal: Huo Yanwei said to Xi: "Among the ten men the sovereign knows, you are the fourth of them—why hesitate!"

units.zh: 習乃從明宗入汴。
units.en: Fu Xi then followed Mingzong into Bian.
units.literal: Xi then followed Mingzong into Bian.

units.zh: 明宗即位，加兼侍中，令歸本鎮。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne Fu Xi was made concurrent Palace Attendant and ordered back to his command.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne Xi was additionally made palace attendant and ordered to return to his original command.

units.zh: 屬青州守將王公儼拒命，復授天平軍節度使。
units.en: When the Qingzhou garrison commander Wang Gongyan defied orders, Fu Xi was again made military commissioner of Tianping.
units.literal: When the Qing Prefecture garrison commander Wang Gongyan defied orders, he was again granted military commissioner of Tianping.

units.zh: 〈（《宋史·顏衎傳》：天成初，為鄒平令。
units.en: (According to the 《History of Song · Biography of Yan Yan》: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was magistrate of Zouping.
units.literal: (《History of Song · Biography of Yan Yan》 states: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was magistrate of Zouping.

units.zh: 符習初鎮天平，習武臣之廉慎者，以書告屬邑，毋聚斂為獻賀。
units.en: When Fu Xi first took command of Tianping—he was known among military men for integrity—he wrote the subordinate counties forbidding them to levy extra taxes as congratulatory gifts.
units.literal: When Fu Xi first garrisoned Tianping, Xi being among military ministers of integrity and caution, by letter informed the subordinate counties not to gather levies as congratulatory gifts.

units.zh: 衎未領書，以故規行之，尋為吏所訟，習遽召衎笞之，幕客軍吏，咸以為辱及正人，習甚悔焉，即表為觀察判官，且塞前事。）〉
units.en: Yan had not yet received the letter and followed the old custom. Clerks soon brought suit against him. Fu Xi had Yan summoned and flogged. His staff and officers all felt an upright man had been disgraced. Fu Xi deeply regretted it, memorialized to make Yan an administrative aide on his staff, and hushed the affair.)〉
units.literal: Yan had not yet received the letter and by old custom carried it out; soon he was sued by clerks; Xi hastily summoned Yan and flogged him; staff and military clerks all thought it shamed a upright man; Xi greatly regretted it, immediately memorialized to make him administrative aide of the observation commission, and moreover blocked the earlier matter.)〉

units.zh: 四年，移汴州節度使。
units.en: In the fourth year he was transferred to military commissioner of Bianzhou.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to military commissioner of Bian Prefecture.

units.zh: 安重誨素不悅習，會汴人言習厚賦民錢，以代納槁，及納軍租，多收加耗，由是罷歸京師。
units.en: An Chonghui had long disliked Fu Xi. When men of Bian reported that he had levied heavy taxes to pay forage on the people's behalf and collected inflated military rents, he was removed and recalled to the capital.
units.literal: An Chonghui had never been pleased with Xi; when men of Bian said Xi heavily taxed the people's money to pay forage in their stead and in collecting military rents took much extra surcharge, because of this he was dismissed and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：習自恃宿將，議論多抗安重誨，故重誨求其過，奏之。）〉
units.en: (According to the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Fu Xi, trusting in his standing as a veteran commander, often contradicted An Chonghui in council, so Chonghui hunted out his faults and memorialized against him.)〉
units.literal: (《Comprehensive Mirror》 states: Xi relied on himself as an old commander and in discussion often opposed An Chonghui; therefore Chonghui sought his faults and memorialized them.)〉

units.zh: 授太子太師致仕，求歸故裏，許之，乃歸昭慶縣。
units.en: He was granted retirement as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, asked to return home, was permitted, and went back to Zhaoqing County.
units.literal: He was granted retirement as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, requested return to his native place, was permitted, and thus returned to Zhaoqing County.

units.zh: 明宗以其子令謙為趙州刺史。
units.en: Mingzong appointed his son Lingqian prefect of Zhao.
units.literal: Mingzong made his son Lingqian prefect of Zhao Prefecture.

units.zh: 習飛揚痛飲，周遊田里，不集朋徒，不過郡邑，如此累年，中風而卒。
units.en: Fu Xi drank hard, wandered the countryside, kept no circle of followers, and avoided the county towns. After years of this he died of a stroke.
units.literal: Xi drank freely in high spirits, wandered through fields and villages, did not gather companions, did not pass through commandery towns, thus for many years, then died of wind stroke.

units.zh: 贈太師。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 子蒙嗣，位至禮部侍郎。
units.en: His son Meng succeeded him and rose to Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: His son Meng succeeded him and reached the post of vice minister of rites.

units.zh: 烏震，冀州信都人也。
units.en: Wu Zhen came from Xindu in Ji Prefecture.
units.literal: Wu Zhen, a native of Xindu in Ji Prefecture.

units.zh: 少孤，自勤於鄉校。
units.en: Orphaned young, he threw himself into study at the district school.
units.literal: Orphaned in youth, he applied himself diligently at the district school.

units.zh: 弱冠從軍，初為鎮州隊長，以功漸升部將，與符習從征於河上，頗得士心。
units.en: At twenty he entered the army as a squad leader in Zhenzhou, rose by merit to section commander, marched with Fu Xi on the Yellow River campaigns, and won strong loyalty from his men.
units.literal: At weak cap he entered the army, at first was squad leader of Zhen Prefecture, through merit gradually rose to section commander, followed Fu Xi in campaigns along the river, and greatly won the soldiers' hearts.

units.zh: 聞張文禮弑王鎔，誌復主讎，雪泣請行。
units.en: When he heard that Zhang Wenli had murdered Wang Rong, he vowed to avenge his lord, wept aloud, and begged to march.
units.literal: When he heard Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, he resolved to avenge his lord, wept tears of grief, and requested to march.

units.zh: 兵及恒陽，文禮執其母妻洎兒女十口誘之，不回，攻城日急。
units.en: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and children—ten persons in all—to lure him back, but he would not turn aside, and the siege pressed harder day by day.
units.literal: When the army reached Hengyang, Wenli seized his mother, wife, and together with sons and daughters ten mouths to entice him, but he did not turn back; the siege of the city grew daily more urgent.

units.zh: 文禮忿之，鹹割鼻斷腕，不絕於膚，放至軍門，觀者皆不忍正視。
units.en: Wenli in his rage had them mutilated, noses cut and wrists severed, wound upon wound, then sent them to the camp gate. The onlookers could not bear to meet their eyes.
units.literal: Wenli resented this; he had them all cut off their noses and sever their wrists, the wounds unceasing on their flesh, and released them to the army gate; onlookers could not bear to look straight at them.

units.zh: 震一慟而止，憤激奮命，身先矢石。
units.en: Wu Zhen choked back a single sob and drove on, burning with rage he threw himself into the assault and led the charge under arrow and stone.
units.literal: Zhen gave one great grief and stopped, in furious zeal threw his life into the fight, and took the lead before arrows and stones.

units.zh: 鎮州平，以功授震深、趙二州刺史。
units.en: When Zhenzhou fell, Wu Zhen was rewarded with the prefectures of Shen and Zhao.
units.literal: When Zhen Prefecture was pacified, by merit Zhen was granted the prefectures of Shen and Zhao.

units.zh: 其性純質，以清直禦下，在河北獨有政聲，移易州刺史，兼北面水陸轉運、招撫等使。
units.en: Plain and upright by nature, he governed his subordinates with integrity and alone in the Hebei north won a name for good rule. He was moved to Yizhou and made concurrent northern commissioner for water and land transport and pacification.
units.literal: His nature was pure and plain; with integrity and uprightness he governed subordinates; in the Hebei north alone he had a reputation for good government; he was transferred to Yi Prefecture and concurrently made northern commissioner for water and land transport and pacification.

units.zh: 契丹犯塞，漁陽路梗，震率師運糧，三入薊門，擢為河北道副招討，遙領宣州節度使，代房知溫軍於盧台。
units.en: When the Khitan raided the frontier and the road to Yuyang was cut, Wu Zhen led grain convoys through Jimen three times. He was promoted to deputy Hebei campaign commissioner, given titular command of Xuanzhou, and sent to replace Fang Zhiwen at Lutai.
units.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier and the Yuyang route was blocked, Zhen led troops transporting grain, three times entered Jimen, was promoted to deputy campaign commissioner of the Hebei circuit, held titular military commissioner of Xuan Prefecture, and replaced Fang Zhiwen's army at Lutai.

units.zh: 及至軍，會戍兵龍至所部鄴都奉節等軍數千人作亂，未及交印而遇害。
units.en: When he reached camp, several thousand garrison troops of the Yedu Fengjie army under Long Zhi mutinied. He was killed before he could even take command.
units.literal: When he reached the army, garrison troops under Long Zhi of the Yedu Fengjie and other armies, several thousand men, mutinied; before he could hand over the seal he met calamity.

units.zh: 明宗聞之，廢朝一日，詔贈太傅。
units.en: Mingzong suspended court for a day on hearing the news and by edict posthumously honored him as Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Mingzong heard of it he suspended court for one day and by edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 震略涉書史，尤嗜《左氏傳》，好為詩，善筆劄，凡郵亭佛寺，多有留題之跡。
units.en: Wu Zhen had some learning in history, loved the Zuo Commentary above all, wrote poetry, and penned fine letters. Post stations and temples all over the north still bore his inscriptions.
units.literal: Zhen had slight acquaintance with books and histories, especially loved the Zuo Commentary, delighted in composing poetry, was skilled at letters, and at every post station and Buddhist temple there were many traces of inscriptions he left.

units.zh: 及其遇禍，燕、趙之士皆歎惜之。
units.en: When he was killed, men of worth in Yan and Zhao mourned him.
units.literal: When he met calamity, gentlemen of Yan and Zhao all sighed in regret.

units.zh: 王瓚，故河中節度使重盈之諸子也。
units.en: Wang Zan was one of the sons of the former Hezhong military commissioner Wang Chongying.
units.literal: Wang Zan was a son among the sons of the former Hezhong military commissioner Chongying.

units.zh: 天復初，梁祖既平河中，追念王氏舊恩，辟瓚為賓佐。
units.en: Early in the Tianfu era, after the Liang Founder pacified Hezhong, he recalled the Wang family's old kindness and took Wang Zan into his staff.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, after the Founder had pacified Hezhong, recalling the Wang family's old favor, he recruited Zan as a guest aide.

units.zh: 梁祖即位，曆諸衛大將軍、兗華兩鎮節度使、開封尹。
units.en: After the Founder took the throne, Wang Zan rose through the guard commands to military commissioner of Yan and Hua and mayor of Kaifeng.
units.literal: When the Founder took the throne Zan served as great general of the guards, military commissioner of the two commands of Yan and Hua, and mayor of Kaifeng.

units.zh: 貞明五年，代賀瑰統軍駐於河上。
units.en: In the fifth year of Zhenming he replaced He Gui as commander of the army on the Yellow River.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Zhenming he replaced He Gui in commanding the army stationed on the river.

units.zh: 時李存審築壘於德勝渡。
units.en: Li Cunshen was then building fortifications at Desheng Ford.
units.literal: At the time Li Cunshen was building stockades at Desheng Ford.

units.zh: 秋八月，瓚率汴軍五萬，自黎陽渡河，將掩擊魏州，明宗出師拒之。
units.en: In the eighth month Wang Zan led fifty thousand Bian troops across from Liyang, intending to strike Wei Prefecture by surprise. Mingzong marched out to meet him.
units.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Zan led fifty thousand Bian troops, crossed the river from Liyang, and was about to strike secretly at Wei Prefecture; Mingzong marched out to resist.

units.zh: 瓚至頓丘而旋，於楊村夾河築壘，架浮航，自滑饋運相繼。
units.en: Wang Zan turned back at Dunqiu, built paired camps at Yangcun on the river, threw pontoon bridges across, and fed his army by continuous convoys from Hua.
units.literal: Zan reached Dunqiu and turned back, at Yangcun built stockades on both sides of the river, erected pontoon bridges, and from Hua supplied transport in succession.

units.zh: 瓚嚴於軍法，令行禁止，然機略應變，則非所長。
units.en: Wang Zan enforced military law with iron discipline, but strategy and improvisation were not his gifts.
units.literal: Zan was strict in military law; orders went forth and prohibitions stood, yet stratagem and adaptation to change were not his strengths.

units.zh: 十一月，瓚率其眾觀兵於戚城，明宗以前鋒擊之，獲其將李立。
units.en: In the eleventh month Wang Zan paraded his army at Qi City. Mingzong's vanguard struck and captured his general Li Li.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Zan led his masses to display arms at Qi City; Mingzong with the vanguard struck them and captured his general Li Li.

units.zh: 十二月，邏騎報汴之饋糧千計，沿河而下，可掩而取之。
units.en: In the twelfth month scouts reported thousands of Bian grain barges moving downriver, ripe for ambush.
units.literal: In the twelfth month patrol horsemen reported Bian supply grain in thousands, moving down along the river, which could be seized by surprise.

units.zh: 莊宗遣徒兵五千，設伏以待之，使騎軍循河南岸西上，俘獲饋役數千。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent five thousand foot soldiers to lie in wait and cavalry up the south bank, seizing several thousand supply men.
units.literal: Zhuangzong sent five thousand foot soldiers to set an ambush and wait, and had cavalry follow the south bank of the river westward, capturing several thousand supply workers.

units.zh: 瓚結陣河曲，以待王師，既而兵合，一戰敗之。
units.en: Wang Zan drew up his line at a bend of the river to await the Tang army. When the forces met, a single battle broke him.
units.literal: Zan formed battle lines at the river bend to await the imperial army; soon the armies joined and in one battle defeated him.

units.zh: 瓚眾走保南城，瓚以小舟北渡僅免。
units.en: His army fled into the southern citadel while Wang Zan himself escaped north in a small boat by a hair's breadth.
units.literal: Zan's masses fled to hold the south city; Zan in a small boat crossed north and barely escaped.

units.zh: 是日，獲馬千餘匹，俘斬萬級，王師乘勝徇地曹、濮。
units.en: That day they took more than a thousand horses and killed or captured ten thousand men. The Tang army swept on through Cao and Pu.
units.literal: That day they captured more than a thousand horses and took or killed ten thousand ranks; the imperial army pressed the victory through Cao and Pu.

units.zh: 梁主以瓚失律，令戴思遠代還。
units.en: The Liang emperor removed Wang Zan for the defeat and sent Dai Siyuan to replace him.
units.literal: The Liang sovereign because Zan lost discipline ordered Dai Siyuan to replace him and return.

units.zh: 及王師襲汴，時瓚為開封府尹。
units.en: When the Tang army struck at Bian, Wang Zan was mayor of Kaifeng.
units.literal: When the imperial army raided Bian, at the time Zan was mayor of the Kaifeng prefecture.

units.zh: 梁主聞王師將至，自登建國門樓，日夜垂泣，時持國寶謂瓚曰：「吾終保有此者，係卿耳。」
units.en: Hearing the Tang army was near, the Liang emperor climbed the Jianguo Gate tower and wept day and night. Clutching the imperial regalia he told Wang Zan, "Whether I keep these treasures at last depends on you alone."
units.literal: The Liang sovereign heard the imperial army was about to arrive, himself ascended the Jianguo Gate tower, wept day and night, and at the time holding the state treasures said to Zan: "My finally keeping these depends on you alone."

units.zh: 令瓚閱市人散徒，登城為備。
units.en: He ordered Wang Zan to disperse the townspeople, man the walls, and prepare the defense.
units.literal: He ordered Zan to review the market people and disperse laborers, ascend the walls and make preparations.

units.zh: 洎明宗至封丘門，瓚開門迎降。
units.en: When Mingzong reached the Fengqiu Gate, Wang Zan opened the gates and surrendered.
units.literal: When Mingzong reached the Fengqiu Gate, Zan opened the gate and welcomed surrender.

units.zh: 翌日，莊宗禦元德殿，瓚與百官待罪及進幣馬，詔釋之，仍令收梁主屍，備槥櫝權厝於佛寺，漆首函送於郊社。
units.en: The next day Zhuangzong held court at the Yuande Hall. Wang Zan and the officials awaited judgment and presented tribute. Zhuangzong pardoned them, ordered the Liang emperor's body collected, placed the coffin provisionally in a temple, and sent the lacquered head in a case to the suburban altars.
units.literal: The next day Zhuangzong held court at the Yuande Hall; Zan with the hundred officials awaited punishment and presented tribute silks and horses; an edict released them, and still ordered collection of the Liang sovereign's corpse, preparation of a coffin for temporary placement in a Buddhist temple, lacquering the head and sending it in a case to the suburban altars.

units.zh: 居數日，段凝上疏奏：「梁朝掌事權者趙岩等，並助成虐政，結怨於人，聖政惟新，宜誅首惡，以謝天下。」
units.en: Days later Duan Ning memorialized, "Zhao Yan and the other men who wielded power in the Liang court helped build a cruel regime and earned the hatred of the realm. Your new rule should cut down the chief culprits to satisfy the world."
units.literal: After several days Duan Ning submitted a memorial stating: "Among those who held power in affairs in the Liang court, Zhao Yan and others all helped complete tyrannical government and formed resentments in men; the sage government is newly renewed—it is fitting to execute the chief evildoers to answer to all under Heaven."

units.zh: 於是張漢傑、張漢融、張漢倫、張希逸、趙縠、朱珪等並族誅，家財籍沒。
units.en: Zhang Hanjie, Zhang Hanrong, Zhang Hanlun, Zhang Xiyi, Zhao Gu, Zhu Gui, and their kin were executed to the last house, and their estates were confiscated.
units.literal: Thereupon Zhang Hanjie, Zhang Hanrong, Zhang Hanlun, Zhang Xiyi, Zhao Gu, Zhu Gui, and others were all exterminated by clan; family wealth was registered and confiscated.

units.zh: 瓚聞諸族當法，憂悸失次，每出則與妻子訣別。
units.en: Hearing that whole clans were to be punished, Wang Zan was sick with fear and bade his wife and children farewell each time he left the house.
units.literal: When Zan heard the clans were to face the law he was anxious and flustered out of order; each time he went out he took leave of his wife and children.

units.zh: 郭崇韜遣人慰譬之，詔授宣武軍節度副使，知府事，檢校太傅如故。
units.en: Guo Chongtao sent envoys to reassure him. An edict made him deputy military commissioner of Xuanwu, in charge of the prefecture, with his acting rank of Grand Mentor unchanged.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao sent men to comfort and instruct him; an edict appointed him deputy military commissioner of the Xuanwu army, in charge of prefectural affairs, with acting grand mentor as before.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》云：瓚伏地請死，莊宗勞而起之曰：「朕與卿家世婚姻，然人臣各為主耳，復何罪邪！」
units.en: (According to Ouyang Xiu's history: Wang Zan prostrated himself and begged for death. Zhuangzong raised him and said, "Our houses have been joined by marriage for generations. A minister serves his own lord. What crime is that?")
units.literal: (The History of Ouyang states: Zan prostrated himself requesting death; Zhuangzong consoled him and raised him, saying: "I and your house are marriage kin for generations, yet ministers each serve their lord—what crime again!"

units.zh: 因以為開封尹，遷宣武軍節度使。）〉
units.en: He then made him mayor of Kaifeng and later military commissioner of Xuanwu.)〉
units.literal: He therefore made him mayor of Kaifeng and transferred him to military commissioner of the Xuanwu army.)〉

units.zh: 瓚心憂疑成疾，十二月卒。
units.en: Anxiety and dread brought on illness, and he died in the twelfth month.
units.literal: Zan's heart, anxious and doubtful, became illness; in the twelfth month he died.

units.zh: 贈太子太師。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 瓚雖為治嚴肅，而慘酷有家世風。
units.en: Though Wang Zan governed with stern discipline, cruelty ran in his family line.
units.literal: Although Zan in governing was stern and solemn, cruelty had a family tradition.

units.zh: 自曆守蕃鎮，頗能除盜，而明不能照下。
units.en: In frontier commands he was effective against bandits, but he could not see clearly what his subordinates were doing.
units.literal: From serving as defender of frontier commands he was quite able to eliminate bandits, yet his clarity could not illuminate subordinates.

units.zh: 及尹正京邑，委政於愛婿牙將辛廷蔚，曲法納賄，因緣為奸。
units.en: As mayor of the capital he handed affairs to his son-in-law and guard officer Xin Tingwei, who bent the law for bribes and used his post for every kind of fraud.
units.literal: When he governed the capital as mayor he entrusted government to his beloved son-in-law guard officer Xin Tingwei, who bent the law to accept bribes and used opportunities to commit villainy.

units.zh: 初，汴人駐軍於河上，軍計不足，瓚請率汴之富戶，出助軍錢，賦取不均，人靡控訴，至有雉經者，又有富室致賂幸而免率者。
units.en: Earlier, when Bian troops were stationed on the river and funds ran short, Wang Zan levied the wealthy households of Bian for war money. The assessments were unfair, appeals went nowhere, some men hanged themselves, and rich families bought exemption with bribes.
units.literal: At first when Bian men were stationed on the river the army accounts were insufficient; Zan requested to lead Bian's wealthy households to contribute military funds; levies were unequal, men had none who could appeal, until some hanged themselves, and some wealthy houses paid bribes and by luck were exempted from the levy.

units.zh: 及明宗即位，素知廷蔚之奸，乃勒歸田里。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne he already knew Xin Tingwei's corruption and sent him back to the countryside.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he had long known Tingwei's villainy and therefore ordered him back to the fields and villages.

units.zh: 然瓚能優禮搢紳，抑挫豪猾，故當時士流皆稱仰焉。
units.en: Yet Wang Zan honored the gentry and checked the bullying powerful, so men of standing in his day still spoke well of him.
units.literal: Yet Zan could treat gentry with generous ceremony and suppress overbearing scoundrels; therefore men of the time in official circles all praised and looked up to him.

units.zh: 袁象先，宋州下邑人也。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian came from Xiayi in Song Prefecture.
units.literal: Yuan Xiangxian was a native of Xiayi in Song Prefecture.

units.zh: 自稱唐中宗朝中書令、南陽郡王恕己之後。
units.en: He claimed descent from Shuji, who had served as Secretariat Director and Prince of Nanyang under Emperor Zhongzong of Tang.
units.literal: He claimed descent from Shuji, Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Nanyang during the reign of Emperor Zhongzong of Tang.

units.zh: 曾祖進朝，成都少尹，梁以象先貴，累贈左僕射。
units.en: His great-grandfather Jinchao had been Vice Prefect of Chengdu. When Xiangxian rose to eminence, the Liang court repeatedly posthumously honored him as Left Vice Minister.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Jinchao was Vice Prefect of Chengdu; because of Xiangxian's eminence, the Liang court repeatedly posthumously honored him as Left Vice Minister.

units.zh: 祖忠義，忠武軍節度判官，累贈司空。
units.en: His grandfather Zhongyi had served as administrative aide to the Zhongwu military commissioner and was posthumously promoted to Minister of Works.
units.literal: His grandfather Zhongyi was administrative aide to the Zhongwu military commissioner; was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

units.zh: 父敬初，太府卿，累贈司徒、駙馬都尉。
units.en: His father Jingchu had served as Minister of the Grand Treasury and was posthumously honored as Minister of Ceremonial and Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.
units.literal: His father Jingchu was Minister of the Grand Treasury; was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Ceremonial and Commissioner of the Imperial Son-in-Law's Household.

units.zh: 敬初娶梁祖之妹，初封沛郡太君。
units.en: Jingchu married the Liang Founder's younger sister, who was first titled Grand Lady of Pei.
units.literal: Jingchu married the Liang Founder's younger sister, who was first enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Pei Prefecture.

units.zh: 開平中，追封長公主。
units.en: During Kaiping she was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Princess.
units.literal: During Kaiping, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess.

units.zh: 貞明中，追封萬安大長公主。
units.en: During Zhenming she was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Princess of Wan'an.
units.literal: During Zhenming, she was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Wan'an.

units.zh: 象先即梁祖之甥也。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew (his sister's son).
units.literal: Xiangxian was the Liang Founder's nephew (his sister's son).

units.zh: 性寬厚，不忤於物，幼遇亂，慨然有憂時之意。
units.en: He was generous by nature and easy with the world. He grew up amid chaos and early felt a patriot's sorrow for the times.
units.literal: His nature was generous and broad, not offensive toward things; in youth he met turmoil and with emotion had the will to worry for the age.

units.zh: 象先嘗射一水鳥，不中，箭落水中，下貫雙鯉，見者異之。
units.en: Once Yuan Xiangxian shot at a water bird and missed. The arrow fell into the river and pierced two carp beneath the surface. Onlookers took it as an omen.
units.literal: Xiangxian once shot a water bird and missed; the arrow fell into the water and pierced downward through a pair of carp; viewers found it strange.

units.zh: 梁祖鎮夷門，象先起家授銀青光祿大夫、檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞。
units.en: When the Founder held Yimen, Yuan Xiangxian entered service as Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Guest of the Heir Apparent, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: When the Founder garrisoned Yimen, Xiangxian began his career granted Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting guest of the Heir Apparent, and concurrent censor-in-chief.

units.zh: 景福元年，自檢校左省常侍，遷檢校工部尚書，充元從馬軍指揮使兼左靜邊都指揮使。
units.en: In the first year of Jingfu he rose from acting Regular Attendant of the Left Secretariat to acting Minister of Works, commander of the Founder's personal horse guard, and concurrent commander of the Left Quiet-the-Border army.
units.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, from acting regular attendant of the left secretariat he was transferred to acting minister of works, made commander of the personal following horse army and concurrent commander of the left Quiet-the-Border command.

units.zh: 乾寧五年，再遷檢校右僕射、左領軍衛將軍同正，充宣武軍內外馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: In the fifth year of Qianning he was made acting Right Vice Director, full-rank commander of the Left Army of Inspired Leadership, and overall commander of the Xuanwu army's horse and foot forces.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Qianning he was again transferred to acting right vice director, left commander of the Army of Inspired Leadership with full rank, and made overall commander of the Xuanwu army's inner and outer horse and foot forces.

units.zh: 光化二年，權知宿州軍州事。
units.en: In the second year of Guanghua he was made acting administrator of Suzhou.
units.literal: In the second year of Guanghua he was acting in charge of Su Prefecture military and civil affairs.

units.zh: 天復元年，表授刺史，充本州團練、埇橋鎮遏都知兵馬使。
units.en: In the first year of Tianfu he was appointed prefect by memorial, regimental trainer of the prefecture, and overall military commander of the Yongqiao garrison.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianfu he was appointed by memorial as prefect, made regimental trainer of the prefecture and overall commander of Yongqiao garrison suppression knowing military affairs.

units.zh: 會淮寇大至，圍迫州城，象先雘力禦備，時援兵未至，頗懷憂沮。
units.en: When Huai rebels came in force and pressed the city, Yuan Xiangxian strained every nerve to defend it. Relief had not arrived, and his spirits sank.
units.literal: When Huai bandits came in great force and pressed the siege on the prefectural city, Xiangxian strove with all strength in defense; at the time relief troops had not arrived and he was quite anxious and dejected.

units.zh: 一日，登北城，憩其樓堞之上，怳然若寢，夢人告曰：「我陳璠也，嘗板築是城，舊第猶在，今為軍舍，可為我立廟，即助公陰兵。」
units.en: One day on the north wall he rested on the parapet and fell into a trance. A figure in a dream said, "I am Chen Fan. I helped build this wall. My old house still stands, now a barracks. Build me a shrine and I will send you hidden troops."
units.literal: One day he ascended the north wall and rested on its parapet; dimly as if asleep a man in a dream told him: "I am Chen Fan. I once rammed earth to build this city; my old residence still stands, now a military quarters—you can build a temple for me, and I will aid you with hidden troops."

units.zh: 象先納之。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian agreed.
units.literal: Xiangxian accepted this.

units.zh: 翌日，淮寇急攻其壘，梯衝角進，是日州城幾陷。
units.en: The next day the Huai rebels stormed the ramparts with ladders and rams, and the city nearly fell that day.
units.literal: The next day Huai bandits fiercely attacked his stockade; scaling ladders and battering rams advanced corner by corner; that day the prefectural city nearly fell.

units.zh: 頃之，有大風雨，居民望見城上兵甲無算，寇不能進，即時退去。
units.en: Then a great storm broke. Townsfolk saw countless armed men on the walls. The rebels could not advance and withdrew at once.
units.literal: Shortly there was great wind and rain; residents looking up saw on the wall armor and weapons beyond counting; the bandits could not advance and at once withdrew.

units.zh: 象先方信鬼神之助，乃為之立祠，至今里人禱祝不輟。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian then believed the spirits had helped him, built Chen Fan a shrine, and local people pray there to this day.
units.literal: Xiangxian then believed in the spirits' aid and therefore built a shrine for him; to this day village people pray without ceasing.

units.zh: 三年，權知洺州軍州事。
units.en: In the third year he was made acting administrator of Mingzhou.
units.literal: In the third year he was acting in charge of Ming Prefecture military and civil affairs.

units.zh: 天祐三年，授陳州刺史、檢校司空。
units.en: In the third year of Tianyou he was made prefect of Chen and acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianyou he was granted Chen Prefecture and acting minister of works.

units.zh: 是歲，陳州大水，民饑，有物生於野，形類蒲萄，其實可食，貧民賴焉。
units.en: That year a great flood struck Chen and the people starved. A wild plant like a grapevine grew in the fields; its fruit was edible, and the poor lived on it.
units.literal: That year Chen Prefecture had great flood; the people were starving; a thing grew in the wilds shaped like grapes, its fruit edible, and the poor relied on it.

units.zh: 梁開平二年，授左英武軍使，再遷左神武、右羽林統軍。
units.en: In the second year of Liang Kaiping he was made commander of the Left Army of Heroic Martiality, then commander of the Left Army of Divine Martiality and the Right Forest of Feathers.
units.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang he was granted commander of the Left Army of Heroic Martiality, then again transferred to commander of the Left Army of Divine Martiality and the Right Forest of Feathers.

units.zh: 三年，轉右衛上將軍，封汝南縣男。
units.en: In the third year he was made Senior General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Baron of Runan.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to senior general of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Baron of Runan County.

units.zh: 四年，權知宋州留後，到任五月，改天平軍兩使留後。
units.en: In the fourth year he was acting military governor of Song. Five months later he was transferred to acting military governor of Tianping.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was acting in charge of Song Prefecture as military governor; five months after taking office he was changed to acting military governor of the Tianping army's two commissioners.

units.zh: 時鄆境再饑，戶民流散，象先即開倉賑恤，蒙賴者甚眾。
units.en: Famine again ravaged Yan, and the people fled. Yuan Xiangxian opened the granaries at once, and multitudes were saved.
units.literal: At the time the Yan region suffered famine again; household people scattered in flight; Xiangxian immediately opened granaries for relief; those who relied on it were very many.

units.zh: 五年，梁祖北征，以象先為鎮定東南行營都招討應接副使，進封開國伯。
units.en: In the fifth year, on the Founder's northern campaign, Yuan Xiangxian was made deputy liaison commissioner of the southeastern stabilization headquarters and promoted to Founding Baron.
units.literal: In the fifth year the Founder campaigned north; Xiangxian was made deputy liaison commissioner of the southeastern campaign headquarters for stabilization, and advanced to enfeoffment as founding Baron.

units.zh: 領兵攻蓚縣，不克而還。
units.en: He led troops against Tiao County, failed to take it, and withdrew.
units.literal: He led troops to attack Tiao County, did not take it, and returned.

units.zh: 俄奉詔自鄆赴闕，鄆人遮留，毀石橋而不得進，乃自他門而逸。
units.en: Soon he was ordered from Yan to court. The people of Yan blocked him, destroyed the stone bridge, and he escaped through another gate.
units.literal: Soon he received an edict to go from Yan to court; Yan people blocked and detained him, destroyed the stone bridge so he could not advance, and he escaped through another gate.

units.zh: 尋授左龍武統軍兼侍衛親軍都指揮使。
units.en: He was soon made commander of the Left Dragon Martial army and overall commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: Shortly he was granted commander of the Left Dragon Martial army and concurrent overall commander of the palace guard personal army.

units.zh: 乾化三年，與魏博節度使楊師厚合謀，誅朱友珪於洛陽。
units.en: In the third year of Qianhua he conspired with the Weibo military commissioner Yang Shihou and killed Zhu Yougui at Luoyang.
units.literal: In the third year of Qianhua he joined with Weibo military commissioner Yang Shihou in conspiracy and executed Zhu Yougui at Luoyang.

units.zh: 梁末帝即位，以功授檢校太保、同平章事，遙領洪州節度使、行開封尹、判在京馬步諸軍，進封開國公。
units.en: When the Last Emperor of Liang took the throne, Yuan Xiangxian was rewarded with acting Grand Guardian, Grand Councilor, titular command of Hongzhou, acting mayor of Kaifeng, and command of the capital armies, and was advanced to Founding Duke.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang took the throne, by merit he was granted acting grand guardian, Grand Councilor of the Pacification Court, titular military commissioner of Hong Prefecture, acting mayor of Kaifeng, and judge of all horse and foot armies in the capital, and advanced to founding Duke.

units.zh: 四年，授青州節度使，加檢校太傅。
units.en: In the fourth year he was made military commissioner of Qing with the acting rank of Grand Mentor.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was granted military commissioner of Qing Prefecture and advanced to acting grand mentor.

units.zh: 未幾，移鎮宋州，加檢校太尉。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to Song and advanced to acting Grand Commandant.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to garrison Song Prefecture and advanced to acting grand commandant.

units.zh: 象先在宋凡十年。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian spent ten years at Song in all.
units.literal: Xiangxian was at Song in all ten years.

units.zh: 初，梁祖領四鎮，統兵十萬，威震天下，關東藩守，皆其將吏，方面補授，由其保薦，四方輿金輦璧，駿奔結轍，納賂於其庭。
units.en: Early on the Founder held four commands and a hundred thousand men, and his might shook the realm. The governors east of the Pass were his officers; regional appointments rode on his recommendation. Gold and jade poured in from every quarter, and gifts crowded his gate.
units.literal: At first the Founder held four commands, commanded a hundred thousand troops, and awed all under Heaven; the frontier defenders east of the Pass were all his generals and clerks; regional appointments and supplements went by his recommendation; from the four directions carts of gold and chariots of jade galloped with wheel tracks joined, presenting bribes at his court.

units.zh: 如是者十餘年，寢成風俗，藩侯牧守，下逮群吏，罕有廉白者，率皆掊斂剝下，以事權門。
units.en: For more than ten years this became custom. From governors down to clerks, few were clean. Nearly all squeezed their subjects to feed the powerful at court.
units.literal: Thus for more than ten years it gradually became custom; feudal lords, prefects, and defenders down to the mass of clerks rarely had integrity; all generally extorted and stripped subordinates to serve the power gate.

units.zh: 象先恃甥舅之勢，所至藩府，侵刻誅求尤甚，以此家財巨萬。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian traded on his kinship with the Founder. In every command he squeezed harder than most, and his household wealth swelled into the millions.
units.literal: Xiangxian relied on the nephew-by-marriage power; wherever he reached a commandery office his encroachment, carving, and exaction were especially severe, and by this his family wealth reached tens of thousands.

units.zh: 莊宗初定河南，象先率先入覲，輦珍幣數十萬，遍賂權貴及劉皇后、伶官巷伯，居旬日，內外翕然稱之。
units.en: When Zhuangzong first secured the south, Yuan Xiangxian was first to court, bringing tribute worth hundreds of thousands. He bribed every powerful man, Empress Liu, the actor-officials, and the palace brokers. Within ten days the court was praising him on every side.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong first secured Henan south of the river, Xiangxian was first to enter audience, transported precious goods in hundreds of thousands, bribed everywhere the powerful and Empress Liu, actor-officials and alley lords; within ten days inner and outer were united in praising him.

units.zh: 初，梁將未復官資者，凡上章奏姓名而已。
units.en: At first, Liang officers who had not yet received new appointments submitted memorials bearing only their names.
units.literal: At first, among Liang generals who had not yet recovered official titles and salaries, whenever they submitted memorials they wrote only their names.

units.zh: 郭崇韜奏曰：「河南征鎮將吏，昭洗之後，未有新官，每上表章，但書名姓，未頒綸製，必負憂疑。」
units.en: Guo Chongtao memorialized, "The officers of the southern commands, after the purge, still hold no new posts. They submit memorials with only their names, and without fresh appointments from the throne they live in anxiety."
units.literal: Guo Chongtao memorialized, saying: "The generals and clerks of the Henan campaign commands, after the great cleansing, have no new offices; each time they submit a memorial they write only name and surname; edicts of appointment have not been issued—they must bear worry and doubt."

units.zh: 即日，復以象先為宋、亳、耀、輝、潁節度使，依前檢校太尉、平章事，仍賜姓，名紹安，尋令歸鎮。
units.en: That same day Yuan Xiangxian was restored as military commissioner of Song, Bo, Yao, Hui, and Ying, with his former ranks of acting Grand Mentor of State and Grand Councilor, granted the imperial surname and the name Shao'an, and soon sent back to his command.
units.literal: That same day Xiangxian was again made military commissioner of Song, Bo, Yao, Hui, and Ying, with former acting grand mentor of state and Grand Councilor as before, still granted the imperial surname with the name Shao'an, and soon ordered to return to his command.

units.zh: 明年，以郊禮，象先復來朝。
units.en: The next year he came to court again for the suburban sacrifice.
units.literal: The next year, because of the suburban sacrifice, Xiangxian again came to court.

units.zh: 是時，製改宋州宣武軍為歸德軍，因侍宴，莊宗謂象先曰：「歸德之名，無乃著題否？」
units.en: Song's Xuanwu command had been renamed Guide-to-Virtue. At a feast Zhuangzong said to him, "Guide-to-Virtue as a name—is it not a little too pointed?"
units.literal: At that time regulations changed Song Prefecture's Xuanwu army to the Guide-to-Virtue army; during attendance at a feast Zhuangzong said to Xiangxian: "The name Guide-to-Virtue—is it not perhaps too pointed?"

units.zh: 象先拜謝而退，即命歸鎮。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian bowed and withdrew, and was ordered back to his command at once.
units.literal: Xiangxian bowed in thanks and withdrew; he was immediately ordered to return to his command.

units.zh: 其年夏，以疾卒於理所，年六十一。
units.en: That summer he died of illness at his headquarters, aged sixty-one.
units.literal: That summer he died of illness at his administrative seat, aged sixty-one.

units.zh: 冊贈太師，周廣順中，贈中書令，追封楚國公。
units.en: By patent he was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Preceptor. Under Later Zhou in the Guangshun era he was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.
units.literal: By patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor; in the Guangshun era of Zhou he was posthumously granted Central Secretariat Director and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.

units.zh: 象先二子，長曰正辭，曆衢、雄二州刺史。
units.en: Yuan Xiangxian had two sons. The elder, Zhengci, served as prefect of Qu and Xiong.
units.literal: Xiangxian had two sons; the elder was named Zhengci and served as prefect of Qu and Xiong prefectures.

units.zh: 次曰{山義}，至周顯德中，終於滄州節度使。
units.en: The younger, Yan, ended his career under Zhou in the Xiande era as military commissioner of Cangzhou.
units.literal: The younger, Yan, ended his career under Zhou in the Xiande era as military commissioner of Cangzhou.

units.zh: 張溫，字德潤，魏州魏縣人也。
units.en: Zhang Wen, whose style name was Derun, came from Wei County in Wei Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhang Wen, style name Derun, was a native of Wei County in Wei Prefecture.

units.zh: 始仕梁祖為步直小將，改崇明都校。
units.en: He first entered the Liang Founder's service as a junior foot-guard officer, then became commander of the Chongming command.
units.literal: He first served the Founder as a junior officer of the foot guard, then was changed to commander of the Chongming command.

units.zh: 貞明初，蔣殷以徐州叛，從劉鄩討平之，改左右捉生都指揮使。
units.en: Early in Zhenming, when Jiang Yin rebelled at Xuzhou, Zhang Wen followed Liu Kun to crush the revolt and was made overall commander of the left and right captive-taking commands.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhenming Jiang Yin rebelled with Xu Prefecture; he followed Liu Kun to attack and pacify him, then was changed to overall commander of the left and right captive-taking commands.

units.zh: 莊宗伐邢台，獲之，用為永清都校，曆武州刺史、山後八軍都將。
units.en: When Zhuangzong attacked Xingzhou he was captured, made commander of the Yongqing command, and served as prefect of Wu and overall commander of the eight armies behind the mountains.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong attacked Xing Prefecture he was captured and employed as commander of the Yongqing command, served as prefect of Wu and overall commander of the eight armies behind the mountains.

units.zh: 從莊宗襲契丹於幽州，收新州，曆銀槍效義都指揮使，再任武州刺史。
units.en: He followed Zhuangzong's raid on the Khitan at Youzhou, recovered Xinzhou, commanded the Silver Spear Loyalty army, and again held Wu Prefecture.
units.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in raiding the Khitan at You Prefecture, recovered Xin Prefecture, served as commander of the Silver Spear Loyalty command, and again held Wu Prefecture.

units.zh: 同光初，契丹陷媯、儒、檀、順、平、薊六州，武州獨全，改授蔚州刺史。
units.en: At the opening of Tongguang the Khitan took Gui, Ru, Tan, Shun, Ping, and Ji. Wu alone stood intact, and Zhang Wen was transferred to Yuzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang the Khitan took the six prefectures of Gui, Ru, Tan, Shun, Ping, and Ji; Wu alone remained intact; he was changed and granted Yu Prefecture.

units.zh: 天成初，曆振武、昭武留後，尋授利州節度使，入為右衛上將軍。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he was acting governor of Zhenwu and Zhaowu, then military commissioner of Lizhou, and entered court as Senior General of the Right Guard.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he served as acting governor of Zhenwu and Zhaowu, soon was granted military commissioner of Li Prefecture, and entered the capital as senior general of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 無幾，授洋州節度使、右龍武統軍，改雲州節制。
units.en: Before long he was made military commissioner of Yang and commander of the Right Dragon Martial army, then controller of Yunzhou.
units.literal: Before long he was granted military commissioner of Yang Prefecture and commander of the Right Dragon Martial army, then changed to controller of Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 清泰初，屯兵雁門，逐契丹出塞，移鎮晉州，嬰疾而卒。
units.en: Early in Qingtai he camped at Yanmen, drove the Khitan beyond the frontier, was transferred to Jinzhou, fell ill, and died.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he encamped troops at Yanmen, drove the Khitan beyond the frontier, was transferred to garrison Jin Prefecture, fell ill, and died.

units.zh: 詔贈太尉。
units.en: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of Grand Commandant.
units.literal: By edict he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor of State.

units.zh: 李紹文，鄆州人，本姓張，名從楚。
units.en: Li Shaowen came from Yan Prefecture. His original surname was Zhang and his given name Congchu.
units.literal: Li Shaowen, a native of Yan Prefecture, originally surnamed Zhang with the given name Congchu.

units.zh: 少事朱瑄為帳下，瑄敗，歸於梁祖，為四鎮牙校，累典諸軍。
units.en: In youth he served Zhu Xuan on his staff. When Xuan fell he entered the Liang Founder's service as an officer of the four commands and rose through repeated army commands.
units.literal: In youth he served Zhu Xuan in his tent staff; when Xuan was defeated he returned to the Founder, became a guard officer of the four commands, and repeatedly held command of armies.

units.zh: 天祐八年，從王景仁戰，敗於柏鄉，紹文與別將曹儒收殘眾，退保相州。
units.en: In the eighth year of Tianyou he fought under Wang Jingren and was defeated at Bai Township. Li Shaowen and the officer Cao Ru gathered the survivors and fell back to Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the eighth year of Tianyou he followed Wang Jingren in battle, was defeated at Bai Township; Shaowen with the separate general Cao Ru gathered the remnant masses and withdrew to hold Xiang Prefecture.

units.zh: 王師之攻魏州也，紹文率眾自黎陽將渡河。
units.en: When the Tang army besieged Weizhou, Li Shaowen led his troops from Liyang to cross the river.
units.literal: When the imperial army attacked Wei Prefecture, Shaowen led his masses from Liyang and was about to cross the river.

units.zh: 時汴人大恐，河無舟楫，紹文懼為王師所逼，乃剽黎陽、臨河、內黃至魏州，歸於莊宗。
units.en: The Bian army was in panic and the river had no boats. Fearing the Tang advance, Li Shaowen plundered his way from Liyang through Linhe and Neihuang to Weizhou and surrendered to Zhuangzong.
units.literal: At the time Bian men were greatly afraid; the river had no boats; Shaowen feared being pressed by the imperial army, therefore raided Liyang, Linhe, and Neihuang to Wei Prefecture and returned to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗嘉納之，賜姓名，分其兩將三千人為左右匡霸軍旅，仍令紹文、曹儒分將之。
units.en: Zhuangzong welcomed him, granted him the imperial surname and personal name, and formed his three thousand men and two officers into the Left and Right Support-the-Hegemon brigades under Shaowen and Cao Ru.
units.literal: Zhuangzong praised and accepted him, granted the imperial surname and name, divided his two generals' three thousand men into left and right Support-the-Hegemon army brigades, and still ordered Shaowen and Cao Ru to divide command of them.

units.zh: 從周德威討劉守光，進檢校司空，移將匡衛軍。
units.en: He followed Zhou Dewei against Liu Shouguang, was promoted to acting Minister of Works, and was given command of the Support-the-Guard army.
units.literal: He followed Zhou Dewei in attacking Liu Shouguang, was advanced to acting minister of works, and was transferred to command the Support-the-Guard army.

units.zh: 十二年，授博州刺史，預破劉鄩於故元城，曆貝、隰、代三郡刺史，領天雄軍馬步副都將，屯於德勝。
units.en: In the twelfth year he was made prefect of Bo, helped defeat Liu Kun at the old Yuan City, served as prefect of Bei, Xi, and Dai, became deputy overall commander of the Tianxiong army, and encamped at Desheng.
units.literal: In the twelfth year he was granted Bo Prefecture, took part in defeating Liu Kun at the old Yuan City, served as prefect of the three commanderies of Bei, Xi, and Dai, held the post of deputy overall commander of the Tianxiong army horse and foot, and encamped at Desheng.

units.zh: 從閻寶討張文禮，為馬步軍都虞候。
units.en: He followed Yan Bao against Zhang Wenli and was made overall adjutant of the horse and foot forces.
units.literal: He followed Yan Bao in attacking Zhang Wenli and was made overall adjutant of the horse and foot army.

units.zh: 明宗收鄆州，以紹文為右都押衙、馬步軍都將，從破王彥章於中都。
units.en: When Mingzong took Yanzhou, Li Shaowen was made right chief capital guard officer and overall commander of the horse and foot forces, and helped break Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu.
units.literal: When Mingzong took Yan Prefecture, Shaowen was made right chief capital guard officer and overall commander of the horse and foot army, and followed in defeating Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu.

units.zh: 同光中，曆徐、滑二鎮副使，知府事。
units.en: During Tongguang he served as deputy commissioner of Xu and Hua and managed their civil affairs.
units.literal: In the Tongguang era he served as deputy commissioner of the two commands of Xu and Hua and managed prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 三年，從郭崇韜討西川，為洋州節度留後，領鎮江軍節度。
units.en: In the third year he followed Guo Chongtao into western Shu, was made acting military commissioner of Yang, and held titular command of the Zhenjiang army.
units.literal: In the third year he followed Guo Chongtao in attacking western Shu, was made acting military commissioner of Yang Prefecture, and held titular military commissioner of the Zhenjiang army.

units.zh: 天成初，為武信軍節度使，尋卒於鎮。
units.en: Early in Tiancheng he was made military commissioner of Wuxin and soon died in office.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was military commissioner of the Wuxin army; soon he died at his command.

units.zh: 史臣曰：昔丁會之事梁祖也，功既隆矣，禍將及矣，挺身北首，故亦宜然。
units.en: The historiographer writes: When Ding Hui served the Liang Founder, his merit had grown great and ruin was closing in. He turned north to save himself, and that much is understandable.
units.literal: The historiographer states: In old times when Ding Hui served the Liang Founder, his merit was already lofty and calamity was about to reach him; he threw his body northward—thus it was also fitting.

units.zh: 然食人之祿，豈合如是哉！
units.en: Yet he had eaten his lord's bread. How could such conduct be right?!
units.literal: Yet having eaten another's salary, how could it be fitting thus!

units.zh: 閻寶再降於人，夫何足貴焉。
units.en: Yan Bao surrendered twice. What is there to admire in that?
units.literal: Yan Bao twice surrendered to others—how is he worth honoring.

units.zh: 符習雪故主之沉冤，享通侯之貴位，乃趙之奇士也。
units.en: Fu Xi avenged his murdered lord and rose to a marquis's rank. He was a rare man of Zhao.
units.literal: Fu Xi wiped away his old lord's deep grievance and enjoyed the noble rank of full marquis—he was a rare gentleman of Zhao.

units.zh: 烏震不憫其親，仁斯鮮矣，雖慕樂羊之跡，豈事文侯之宜。
units.en: Wu Zhen showed no pity for his kin, and humanity was thin in him. Although he admired Yue Yang's example, how was that a fitting way to serve Marquis Wen.
units.literal: Wu Zhen did not pity his kin; humanity was scarce in him. Although he admired Yue Yang's track, how was serving Marquis Wen fitting.

units.zh: 瓚洎象先而下，皆降將也，又何足以譏焉！
units.en: Wang Zan, Yuan Xiangxian, and the rest were all men who had surrendered. What point is there in dwelling on their faults?!
units.literal: Zan down to Xiangxian and below were all surrendering generals—what again is sufficient to criticize!
